findings.title: Progress 'achievements' cookie exchanged with apo-games.de cookies.php over plain HTTP
findings.entry_point: HTTP response body of http://www.apo-games.de/apoSudoku/cookies.php (PROGRAM_URL, ApoSimpleSudokuConstants.java:28), read by ApoHelp.loadData (org/apogames/help/ApoHelp.java:446-474, readLine at :465)
findings.sink: Parsing loop at ApoSimpleSudokuLevelChooser.java:144-155 adds each comma-separated integer to this.solvedLevels (line 148); saveCookies() sends the same state back in cleartext (line 166 -> ApoHelp.saveData, ApoHelp.java:419-444)
findings.data_path: init() (LevelChooser.java:39) spawns a thread (line 67-72) -> loadCookies() (line 133) -> ApoHelp.loadData(new URL(PROGRAM_URL), COOKIE_NAME) (line 137) -> loadData builds new URL(codebase + "cookies.php") (ApoHelp.java:452), openConnection() over http:// (:454), reads first response line (:465) -> returned String split on ',' and Integer.valueOf'd into solvedLevels (LevelChooser.java:146-149). Outbound path: solveLevel() -> saveCookies() (159) -> saveData (166) -> writes "SET=&name=apoSudoku_level&value=<levels>" to the connection output stream (ApoHelp.java:420-432)
findings.attack_scenario: (1) Player runs the applet build (B_APPLET=true, set in ApoSimpleSudokuApplet.java:26 / ApoScreen.initApplet():162). On the level-chooser screen the client GETs cookies.php and later uploads solved-level IDs. (2) An on-path attacker (open WiFi, malicious ISP) or whoever controls/resolves www.apo-games.de (the domain is long-dead; no TLS, no pinning, so DNS hijack or expired-domain registration works outright) replies with e.g. '0,1,2,...,30,' and forges the player's solved-level record, or logs the upload to profile gameplay progress. Impact is bounded: solvedLevels only paints overlay circles in the chooser (render(), LevelChooser.java:277-283) - every level button is clickable regardless (mouseReleased(), lines 217-228) - so this is record/privacy tampering, not an unlock.
findings.preconditions: Game must run in applet mode (both loadCookies and saveCookies early-return otherwise, LevelChooser.java:134/:160); attacker needs a network vantage point or control of apo-games.de DNS/registration. Desktop build never issues these requests.
findings.validation_plan: Flip the applet path on (launch ApoSimpleSudokuApplet, or set ApoConstants.B_APPLET=true before init), map www.apo-games.de to 127.0.0.1 in /etc/hosts, run `nc -l 80` or a logging Python http.server. Open the level chooser: observe the raw request containing 'GET=&name=apoSudoku_level' in cleartext; answer with '0,1,2,' and observe red overlays on levels 1-3 - proving both the transport exposure and that server bytes become client game state.

findings.title: Dead-code ApoClassLoader loads and instantiates classes from arbitrary file path or URL
findings.code_excerpt: URLClassLoader cl = new URLClassLoader( new URL[] { url } );
findings.entry_point: None in this variant: a tree-wide grep shows ApoClassLoader is never instantiated (no 'new ApoClassLoader'). By design (see sibling-variant pattern and the leftover '.class'-filter JFileChooser labeled 'load an ai', ApoSimpleSudokuGameComponent.java:29-32/:62-69) it would take a directory/file path or URL plus a class name.
findings.sink: cl.loadClass(this.getClassname()) at line 73 followed by c.newInstance() at line 75 - arbitrary bytecode instantiation; url comes straight from getPath() (line 66: new File(path).toURI().toURL() for desktop, line 68: new URL(path) for applets)
findings.data_path: getMyClass() (line 62) -> path/classname fields set via constructor/setters (19-22, 36-54) -> URLClassLoader over that location (69) -> loadClass (73) -> newInstance (75). Zero intermediate validation of path or classname.
findings.attack_scenario: Not exploitable as shipped in THIS variant because nothing calls it - this is latent cloned library code. If any future/clone wiring passes a user- or download-supplied location (e.g. 'load AI class from disk/network' as in other Apo games), anyone who can place a .class file at that location gets it instantiated inside the game JVM: local tamperer executes code, or a malicious level/AI distribution channel achieves RCE.
findings.preconditions: Someone must add a call site (or ship a sibling variant that has one) whose path/classname argument is influenced outside the trust boundary; then attacker needs write access to that filesystem location or control of that URL/host.
findings.validation_plan: Static proof of dormancy: `grep -rn 'new ApoClassLoader' src/` returns nothing. Dynamic proof of danger if wired: create Evil.class with a constructor calling Runtime.getRuntime().exec("touch /tmp/pwned"), then invoke new ApoClassLoader(<dir-with-Evil>, "Evil").getMyClass(); observe /tmp/pwned created - demonstrating defineClass-equivalent execution from attacker-writable locations with no signature/integrity check.

findings.title: Hand-rolled 'connected' chain-string parser has no length/digit/range validation (currently fed only by compile-time literals)
findings.entry_point: In THIS variant there is none: help.getConnected()[i] originates exclusively from hardcoded String literals in ApoSimpleSudokuLevelMake.java (e.g. lines 75-78); no file, network, or user input reaches it (grep confirms nothing extends ApoIO, so its FileInputStream/URL readLevel path, ApoIO.java:75-96, is never used).
findings.sink: charAt(st+1) at line 114 throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException on odd-length strings; Integer.valueOf at 113-114 throws NumberFormatException on non-digits; this.connected[y][x] = (byte)i at line 116 throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException when a digit exceeds width-1; the lookahead at 121-123 reads charAt(st+3) guarded only by 'st + 2 < connected.length()' - off-by-one crash when length == st+3
findings.data_path: ApoSimpleSudokuLevelMake.getLevel(level) (called from ApoSimpleSudokuGame.init():61) constructs ApoSimpleSudokuLevelHelp(width, connected, level) -> new ApoSimpleSudokuLevel(help) -> init() (level ctor, line 57-60) iterates each connected string two chars at a time (112-155) mapping coordinate pairs into the connected[][] grid. Any malformed element crashes the constructing thread.
findings.attack_scenario: Theoretical in this build: a player cannot influence these strings - they are baked into the jar. The risk materializes only through reuse: the identical Level-class skeleton in sibling variants is fed from downloaded levels (get_level.php / readLevel), where a hostile server or edited level file supplying '00 1'-style odd-length, non-digit, or out-of-range pairs crashes the game thread (denial of service) at exactly this sink.
findings.preconditions: For this variant: none can be met by an attacker - input is compile-time constant. To demonstrate the defect one must edit the source literal or port the parser to a sibling variant that loads levels externally.
findings.validation_plan: Edit one literal in ApoSimpleSudokuLevelMake.getFirstLevel() from "00011021" to "0001102" (odd length), run ApoSimpleSudokuMain and start level 1: observe StringIndexOutOfBoundsException thrown from ApoSimpleSudokuLevel.init line 114 during construction - confirming the parser performs no format validation and fails closed only by accident of its current callers.

categories_checked_and_absent: untrusted_deserialization - no ObjectInputStream, XMLDecoder, or any java.serialization usage anywhere in the 43 files (tree-wide grep); ApoIO streams raw primitives only and nothing implements its abstract parsers

weak_integrity_check - MessageDigest/MD5 exists (ApoHelp.getMd5Digest, ApoHelp.java:313-322) but has zero callers; no score/level validation logic exists at all in this variant, so there is no integrity mechanism to weaken

path_traversal - no user-controlled strings reach File/FileOutputStream/FileInputStream; the only path construction uses fixed System.getProperty("user.dir") defaults behind JFileChoosers (ApoSimpleSudokuGameComponent.java:65/:78/:91) that are themselves never opened (getFileChooser*/getFileChooserEditor have no callers)
credential_or_secret_exposure - no passwords, tokens, keys, or personal identifiers are stored, transmitted, or logged anywhere

resource_exhaustion - no attacker-reachable unbounded loops or allocations; the only remotely-fed parser (LevelChooser.loadCookies:144-155) terminates because each iteration consumes the ',' prefix and catches NumberFormatException
unsafe_native_call - no System.load/loadLibrary, JNI, or ProcessBuilder/Runtime.exec usage

legacy_sandbox_assumption - applet-era code exists (B_APPLET branches) but nothing assumes signed-applet privileges or uses AccessController/doPrivileged; the sandbox-relevant consequence (cleartext cookie persistence) is captured in finding 01
notes: This is the minimal end of the Apo corpus: all 31 puzzles are hardcoded byte arrays in ApoSimpleSudokuLevelMake.java; there are no save/level/replay/cheat files, no get_level.php/save_highscore.php traffic (only the cookies.php achievement sync of finding 01, gated to applet mode), and entry points (ApoSimpleSudokuMain.main, ApoSimpleSudokuApplet.init) ignore args and applet parameters entirely. A large fraction of org.apogames is cloned dead weight here: ApoClassLoader (finding 02), ApoIO (nothing extends it), ApoImage's external File/URL image loading (getImageFromPath/getPic(path,true) never called; all graphics are procedurally drawn), ApoHelp's MD5 and clipboard helpers, and the '.class'/'.rep'/'.skunk' JFileChoosers in ApoSimpleSudokuGameComponent. These unwired clones are precisely how flaws propagate in clone-and-own reuse - the dangerous capability ships in the jar whether or not this game exercises it. Functional quirk worth noting: ApoHelp.saveData/loadData force setRequestMethod("GET") yet write a request body (ApoHelp.java:426/:431), relying on old HttpURLConnection behavior of silently upgrading to POST; on strict stacks the persistence silently breaks.
